Estimate a mixed graphical model (MGM)

Source: R/build_aliases.R
build_mgm.Rd

build_network(method = "mgm"), or for short build_mgm(), estimates a mixed graphical model (MGM) of continuous and categorical variables. The edge between two variables is the strength of their interaction, fitted by penalised node-wise regression with the penalty chosen by EBIC (Haslbeck & Waldorp, 2020).

Factor and character columns are categorical, and an integer column with at most 10 values is categorical with a warning. Missing continuous values are filled with the observed column mean and missing categorical values with the modal level; this keeps the rows and is psychnets' documented na_method = "pairwise" policy, not pairwise deletion.

Usage

build_mgm(
  data,
  actor = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  lambdaGam = 0.25,
  ruleReg = c("AND", "OR"),
  metadata_cols = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  labels = NULL,
  params = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

The variables: a data frame with one row per observation and one column per variable, continuous or categorical.

actor

The id column naming whose observation each row is (a person). With level, the decomposition groups by it; without, it is set aside, not modelled. Default NULL.

level

With actor, a multilevel decomposition ("between", "within" or "both"), as for build_cor(). A numeric vector instead gives one category count per modelled variable (1 for continuous ones); it is checked and kept for compatibility, and the fit reads the categories from the data. Default NULL.

lambdaGam

The EBIC hyperparameter. Default 0.25.

ruleReg

"AND" (default) keeps an edge when both regressions select it, "OR" when either does.

metadata_cols

Columns to keep as the network's metadata (covariates), never read as variables. Default NULL.

group

A column to split the data by: one network per value, returned as a netobject_group. Default NULL.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" rescales the weights to run from 0 to 1, over every cell for the transition methods (tna's rule, so with no zero cell the smallest weight becomes 0) and over the non-zero weights, into (0, 1], for the other methods, "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1; an undirected network whose matrix it makes asymmetric becomes directed, so both of a pair's values are kept as edges. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero (default 0); or "LW" or "none", mgm's rule for thresholding the coefficients (mgm's default is "LW").

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names. Default NULL.

params

Settings for the estimator, as a named list. The network stores them. Default list().

...

Further arguments for build_network(). method cannot be given (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group), as build_network() returns it.

References

Haslbeck, J. M. B., & Waldorp, L. J. (2020). mgm: Estimating time-varying mixed graphical models in high-dimensional data. Journal of Statistical Software, 93(8), 1–46. doi:10.18637/jss.v093.i08

See also

build_network() for every method; build_ising() for binary variables, build_glasso() for continuous ones.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  mixed <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100),
                      g = factor(sample(c("a", "b"), 100, TRUE)))
  build_network(mixed, method = "mgm")
  build_mgm(mixed)
}
#> Network (method: mgm) [undirected]
#> 
#>   No edges: every weight is zero.
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix.
